comment: This class was way too much for a non-intensive Spanish class. Ultimately, there is way too much VHL (2 hours of hw each night) that is simply just busy work. There are multiple pop quizzes that you have no idea are coming. Some easy, some are difficult, so study the words before class. The outline is exactly what will be on the test, no surprises.
She is a very nice woman, but not a great teacher. Will not respond to emails. Ever. About 4-5 hours of VHL homework after each class (3 times a week)

She seems to care about her students, but she also doesn't respond to emails EVER. Participation matters and there is a lot of cold calling. There are quizzes throughout the semester but they are never announced ahead of time. There is at least 2 hours of homework after each class. Drill was annoying.

Hard class in general - fast paced. Be prepared for 1-2 hours of hw every night. Very tedious to do. Exams are clearly outlined in review guides - never any surprises. Participation is key and a lot of cold calling. There are occasional pop quizzes
Very caring, funny, and good teacher - just work-heavy for a 151 Spanish class.

Classes were taught 90% in Spanish with the expectation of students participating in Spanish as well, but it never felt stressful to me. There were MANY tedious homework assignments, but not very difficult. I know some of my classmates disagreed, but I really enjoyed the class and learned a lot. She's funny and caring, just try!

She assigns 30-40 VHL assignments per class which is insane for a 151-level course. You can look up all the answers but it's tedious and you learn nothing. She does include partner work a lot in class which is fun and is a nice lady overall. Study guides are detailed so you can succeed on exams with a little preparation.

Gives way too much homework for a 151 class. I'm doing about a quarter of the work in my 221 class just to get by. Most homework is also VHL busywork that doesn't help you improve. Nice teacher but not very effective at teaching new material and is often unavailable and doesn't respond to emails. Also randomly cancels classes every couple weeks.

Dr. Amaral-Rodriguez is well-meaning but a little impotent when it comes to teaching. She is slightly disorganized but wants students to do well, yet doesn't put in the work to accomplish this. While she has your best intentions at heart, she is at best average. LAIS151 with her was of decent difficulty and overall made for an unremarkable class.

She is the real deal, a professor who challenges you and helps you rise to the challenge. My thinking and argument improved so much in this course, because I went to office hours and listened to her feedback and revised at least twice. Fascinating how imperialism works, great readings and interesting questions and assignments. Awesome profesora!

The class is interesting but the Prof. is not a good professor. The class was hard to follow, it was disorganized and there were too many assignments with not enough feedback. She also canceled class 6-7 times and moved the class to zoom with around short notice 3-4 times. Cares about her students but doesn't devote time or effort to her class.

The discussions about issues in Puerto Rican society and politics were very interesting as well as helping us to learn the language in a much more natural way. Fairly accessible outside class but she has a newborn so she can't devote as much time. Really cares for her students. I just wish those few grammar classes would be just as interesting.

She is a very nice professor and tries hard but makes it very confusing because a different topic is the focus every class. She is a bit disorganized but tries her best to help students and obviously cares about their improvement in the language. Not a bad professor just needs more structure
